method: Direct en.wiktionary.org/w/api.php queries for 100 randomly-sampled K-3 nouns per locale from image-vocabulary.js (seed=42). Coverage = (entries with valid {{IPA|<code>|...}} template in the language section) / sampled count.
threshold: 60% — below this NL would have been treated like DA (defined-quarantine + policy-managed) rather than relying on Wiktionary as load-bearing.

verdict_per_locale.de: Above threshold — Wiktionary IPA usable as a count cross-check source
verdict_per_locale.nl: Above threshold — design-pass concern (estimated 50-70%) did NOT materialize; proceed with normal multi-source gate (4 sources for NL: T + R + W + S)
verdict_per_locale.sv: Above threshold — combined with NST (gold-standard), strongest source stack of all locales
verdict_per_locale.no: Above threshold — combined with NST, robust source stack
verdict_per_locale.da: Above threshold — combined with NST + Juul/Elbro G-P table + da-quarantine regex, sufficient for policy-managed quarantine workflow

fi_special_case.explanation: Finnish Wiktionary entries use a Finnish-specific {{fi-pronunciation}} template that auto-generates IPA from spelling rather than the generic {{IPA|fi|...}} template. We do NOT query Wiktionary for Finnish in the production pipeline because (a) the IPA isn't directly available in the wikitext, and (b) even if resolved, the auto-generated IPA is derived from spelling, so it wouldn't be a TRULY independent source. Finnish's gate uses T (TeX hyphenation) + R (rule-based phonotactic syllabifier) + S (vocab-phonics syl count) = 3 sources, which is the design intent for the GREEN locale.
fi_special_case.earlier_preflight_probe_was_overcounting: The earlier 100-word probe reported 88% Wiktionary coverage for Finnish — this was a measurement bug (the section-end detector matched ===Subheaders=== as well as level-2 ==Headers==, so the regex was effectively checking the whole wikitext for any IPA template, not just the Finnish section). The bug was corrected when building the production adapter.

next_action: Run pipeline on SV + FI as the design's proof locales. SV is the strongest case (NST as gold-standard + Wiktionary as count cross-check); FI is the GREEN control (rule-syllabifier as primary independent source, no NST needed).
